chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, similar to it.
He said, 'I said to Ali ibn al-Hakam, "What is the muwat of the goat?" He said, "That which has become equal, where no part of it is superior to another."'

key_terms.الْمُوَاتُ: The equal or balanced animal, fit for sacrifice

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'al-muwat' mean regarding the condition of a goat for sacrifice?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the physical criteria for 'al-muwat' (the equalized or balanced animal), specifying that a goat is suitable for sacrifice only when its limbs and body parts are symmetrical without disproportionate variation. In Shia fiqh, this definition underscores the importance of physical integrity (karamat al-badan) in ensuring the validity of the offering, distinguishing a sound animal from one with minor defects that might diminish its value.
